**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a snack of whole raw almonds on a small paper plate.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** It is a small white paper plate. Judging from the almond size (each about 2.3–2.5 cm long), the plate is about 18 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 9² ≈ 254 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole almonds only. There is no oil or sauce.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The almonds cover a central patch of about 20% of the plate, roughly 51 cm². Gaps between nuts are visible, and the rest of the plate is empty.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The pile is mostly a single layer with some overlap, about 1.3 cm high. 51 cm² × 1.3 cm ≈ 66 ml gross volume.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Loose whole nuts have a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml, giving 66 × 0.6 ≈ 40 g. As a cross-check, I count about 30–32 almonds at roughly 1.2 g each, which gives about 38 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Almonds have about 579 kcal per 100 g. 38 g × 5.79 ≈ 220 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 30 almonds is a little more than a standard 1 oz (28 g, ~23 almonds) serving. So roughly 38 g and 220 kcal is plausible.
